examples.en: The jacket is hanging on the coat rack.
I'll put the blouse on a hanger.
The phone is on a stand.

related.en: coat rack, hook rail — a stand or a strip with hooks for jackets and coats
clothes hanger — holds a garment by the shoulders in a wardrobe
stand — for a phone, a flower, shoes

examples.en: See you in five minutes.
Turn right in a hundred meters.

examples.sr: На збору је било [пре̏ко] пет стотина људи.
examples.en: There were over five hundred people at the meeting.

related.en: across, over, on the other side of; more than; by means of
in (so much time or distance from now)

note: Пре̏ко means «across» or «more than», never «in (so long)»: пре̏ко мо̏ста, преко пријатеља. «In five minutes, in a hundred meters» is за.

examples.en: I'm thirty-five years old.
I was born in '83.
The car is a 2013 model.

related.en: year, age — with a number: пет година
year of birth, model year — neuter

note: Adults are usually asked Ко̀је̄ си го̀диште?, while Колико имаш година? sounds more like a question to a child.

examples.en: The teacher wrote the grade in the class register.
Bring the pupil's record book to the parent-teacher meeting.

related.en: class register — the teacher's record book
pupil's record book — with the pupil's grades

note: Дне̑внӣк is also a personal diary and a news bulletin.

examples.en: The bus driver stopped at the station.
The guide showed us the old town.
The news presenter announced the guest.

related.en: driver — of a car, a bus
guide, tour guide — shows a city to tourists
TV host, presenter, announcer — hosts a show

note: A driver at the wheel is only во̀за̄ч.

examples.en: What are you doing tonight?
Grandma is making pancakes.
Mom is cooking lunch.
I'm preparing dinner for the guests.

related.en: to make, create, produce — pancakes, a house
to do, to work — the process and the occupation
to cook, boil — soup, porridge
to prepare, get ready — including setting the table

note:
For «to cook lunch» ку̏вати, спре́мати and пра̏вити ру́чак all work, but ку̏вати means specifically to boil.

Ра́дити asks about the activity, пра̏вити about the result.

examples.en: I have to look after my sister.

examples.sr: Ништа не могу да [чу̏је̄м] због буке.
examples.en: I can't hear anything because of the noise.

related.en: to keep, protect, guard, look after
to hear — sounds and news

note:
They sound alike but conjugate differently:
• чу́вати - чувам, чувају, past participle чувао
• чу̏ти - чу̏је̄м, чу̏јӯ, past participle чуо, чула

examples.en: He is an imaginative storyteller.
Our designer is very creative.

related.en: imaginative — invents stories and ideas
creative — makes new things, including by hand

note: Машто̀вит comes from ма̀шта, «imagination».

meanings: крзно, длака, коса - which is which?

examples.en: The cat has soft fur.
There is dog hair everywhere.
She has long dark hair.

related.en: fur — an animal's thick coat, and fur as a material
hair, coat — a single hair, or an animal's hair; on animals and people
hair on a person's head

examples.sr: Одлучила сам да [офа̀рбам] косу у црно.
examples.en: I decided to dye my hair black.
Children love to color pictures.

related.en: to paint, dye — hair, walls, a room
to color, tint — a picture, an object; also figuratively

note: If unsure, use о̀фа̄рбати for hair and walls.

meanings: напунити, наточити, сипати - how to pour and fill

examples.en: Fill the glass to the brim.
Pour me a little water.
Pour the flour into the bowl.

related.en: to fill — to the brim, to full capacity
to pour out a liquid — wine, water, fuel
to pour — the most general: both liquids and loose material

note: На̀пунити is about the result, нато̏чити and си̏пати about the pouring itself. When in doubt, use си̏пати.

meanings: опрости, извини, извињавам се - how to apologize

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't hear you.
Excuse me, I have to go.
I apologize for being late.
I'm sorry I'm late.

related.en: sorry, forgive me — a small slip, friendly tone
excuse me, sorry — all-purpose: among friends and politely to strangers
I apologize — formal, in writing, at work
I'm sorry — regret and sympathy, not necessarily guilt

note: For a small awkwardness there is also «не замери» (no offense).

meanings: какав, овакав, онакав, такав, некакав, икакав, никакав

examples.en: What kind of movie is it?
I've never seen a crowd like this.

examples.sr: Хоћу [она̀ка̄в] ауто као што има комшија.
examples.en: I want a car like the one the neighbor has.
I don't like movies like that.
Some man from the bank is calling you.
Is there any point in waiting at all?
I have no plan for the weekend.
Bring any book.

related.en: what kind of — asks about quality
this kind of — like this one, here and now
that kind of — like that one, far away or earlier
such, that kind of — already mentioned
some kind of — indefinite
any at all — questions and conditions
no ... at all — with a negation
any — whichever you choose

note: All of them decline like adjectives: ка̀ка̄в, каква, какво.

examples.sr: Један [хра́бар] пас је скочио у воду.
examples.en: A brave dog jumped into the water.
Our brave dog guards the yard.

related.en: brave, indefinite form — after «бити», «један», «неки»
brave, definite form — for a specific, known one: «овај», «наш», a name

note:
It is one adjective: the short form introduces something or stands in the predicate, the long one singles out a specific one.

The difference exists only in the masc. sg. nominative, in other cases the forms are the same.

examples.sr: Ово није само кућа, ово је наш [до̏м].
examples.en: This is not just a building, this is our home.
We bought a big house in the country.

related.en: home, hearth, place of origin; an institution: Дом здравља (health center)
house, building — a specific structure

note: «Going home» is кући: идем кући, «at home» is код куће.

examples.en: I'm going to wash the dishes.
First wipe the dust off the shelves.

related.en: to wash — with water: dishes, laundry, hands
to wipe, dust, erase — without immersing: a floor, dust, a table

note: «To do the laundry» is пра̏ти ве̏ш, «to delete a file» is бри̏сати.

examples.en: He sat among the guests.
The restaurant is between two buildings.

related.en: among — inside a group or a multitude
between — two things, at an exact spot

note: И̏змеђу takes the genitive, ме̏ђу the instrumental: и̏змеђу згра̏да, међу зградама.

examples.en: Could I have a glass of white wine?
Bring us a carafe of wine for the table.

related.en: carafe, pitcher — for the table, with wine or water
glass — an individual serving: чаша вина

note: Ask for бо̀ка̄л and you will get a whole carafe of wine.

examples.en: I always kiss my husband goodbye.
I love ćevapi and pljeskavica.

related.en: to kiss — «Љубим те»: «Love, ...» at the end of a letter or text
to love, like — people, food, activities: «Волим те»

note: Љу́бити means only «to kiss». Љубим ћевапе would mean «I kiss the ćevapi».

examples.en: Say hi to Mom for me.
Congratulations on your birthday!

related.en: to give regards, greet, say goodbye
to congratulate on something — a holiday, a birthday

note: По̏здра̄в! is also a plain «hi», with no occasion.

examples.en: In the evening I like to read a book.

examples.sr: Када је учитељ ушао, сви су [ћу̀тали].
examples.en: When the teacher came in, everyone fell silent.

related.en: to read
to be silent

note: They sound alike but mean different things: чѝтати is to read, ћу́тати is to be silent.

examples.en: My son is a third-grader.
He is a medical student.

related.en: pupil, schoolchild — primary and secondary school
student — university, college

note: At a university you say студирам, at school - учим. A female student is сту̀денткиња.

examples.en: Chicken soup is light and warm.

examples.sr: Рибља [чо́рба] је довољна за цео ручак.
examples.en: Fish čorba is enough for a whole lunch.

related.en: clear, light soup, broth — often with vegetables and homemade noodles
thick, hearty soup — big pieces of meat or fish, vegetables, potatoes

note: Чо́рба is almost a dish of its own, while су̏па is more of a first course.

examples.en: Shall we go for coffee? - Sure!
I agree with the content of the contract.

related.en: I agree — everyday: at home, in a café, with colleagues
I agree — formal: contracts, documents

note: In conversation use слажем се, otherwise you will sound like you are at a committee meeting. A woman says сагласна сам.

examples.en: Do you want to try this cake?

examples.sr: Ја ћу [по̀кушати] да објасним граматику једноставно.
examples.en: I will try to explain the grammar simply.

related.en: to try, try on, test — with any object
to attempt — only before an action, usually «да» + verb

note: If a noun follows the verb, only про́бати works. When in doubt, про́бати is safer.

examples.en: You're really talented!
I don't like foreign food.
It's really strange that he didn't come.

related.en: really, truly
foreign, alien, unfamiliar
strange, odd, incomprehensible

note: A trap: «strange» is чу̏дно, while стра̑но means «foreign, unfamiliar»: стра́на хра́на is foreign food.

meanings: ући, изаћи, отићи, скокнути - go in, out, away

examples.en: I went into the house.
I left the house at eight.
I left work at five.
I'll pop over to the store.

related.en: to go in, enter
to go out, exit
to leave, go away — leave a place
to pop over, nip out — for a short while: «до продавнице»

examples.en: After school we go to the cinema.
After dinner they went for a walk.

related.en: after, afterwards — colloquial; can stand without a noun: «идемо после»
after, following — formal: only with a noun

note: Before a whole clause на̀кон needs што̏: након што је завршио посао.

examples.en: I'll pay for the coffee.

examples.sr: [Напла̀тила] је двадесет евра за час српског.
examples.en: She charged twenty euros for a Serbian lesson.

related.en: to pay — the money leaves you: coffee, rent
to charge, collect payment — the money comes to you

note: На̀платити is not the perfective of пла́тити, it is a different verb.

examples.en: Do you have an ID card?
Can I pay by card?

related.en: map, ticket, card — a world map, a ski pass (возна карта), an ID card (лична карта)
small card — a bank card, a SIM card, a greeting card

note: Ка̑рта is also a playing card: играти карте.

examples.en: A bag? - No, thanks.
You do not need to come in person.

related.en: no need, no thanks — colloquial: in a shop, at a market
it is not necessary — formal: a bank, business correspondence

note: In daily speech people say не тре́ба. Није потребно in conversation sounds too ceremonious, like a letter from a ministry.

examples.en: I'm going to the doctor about my throat.
In the stories the healer treated people with herbs.

related.en: doctor, physician — the ordinary word
healer, witch doctor, sorcerer — treats with herbs and spells

examples.en: Where did you park the car?
The car is in front of the building.
You have to get the vehicle inspected.

related.en: car — colloquial, everyday
car — colloquial, always plural
vehicle — official: documents, inspection

note:
Ко̏ла is a neuter plural even though there is one car: Ко̏ла су но̑ва.

Во̀зило is a word from documents, in daily speech it sounds like «footwear» instead of «shoes».

examples.en: What are you studying?
What kind of vegetable is this?
What is this cucumber like?

related.en: what — a general question when nothing is known
which, what — a choice among several
what kind of, what ... like — by quality: a property, an opinion

note: A question about an unknown thing starts with шта̏, and then you narrow it down with ко̀јӣ or ка̀ка̄в.

examples.en: I find it hard to remember dates.

examples.sr: [Се̏ћаш] ли се кад смо путовали у Нови Сад?
examples.en: Do you remember when we traveled to Novi Sad?

related.en: to memorize, remember — put into memory: numbers, dates, passwords
to remember, recall — take out of memory: the past

note: Се̏ћати се takes the genitive: сећам се града.

examples.en: I can lift that, I'm strong.
He is a mighty ruler.

related.en: strong — the ordinary neutral word
mighty, powerful — bookish: epics, fairy tales, a ruler

note: For ordinary strength use ја̑к: ја̑ко де́те, not си̑лно де́те.

examples.sr: Хајде на кафу? - Може, треба ми добар [ра̏згово̄р].
examples.en: Shall we go for coffee? - Sure, I need a good talk.

examples.sr: Његова [бѐседа] на конференцији била је дирљива.
examples.en: His speech at the conference was moving.

related.en: conversation, talk — an ordinary live conversation
speech, sermon — a bookish, solemn address

note: Бѐседа sounds bookish and old-fashioned, like a word from a stage or a church. The verb for ра̏згово̄р is разгова́рати.

examples.en: I like to cook, but I have no time.
This is not a glass but a cup.

examples.sr: Не зато што нећу, [ве̏ћ] зато што не могу.
examples.en: Not because I don't want to, but because I can't.

related.en: but — contrasts two thoughts
but rather — after a negation; also «than»
but rather — after a negation, more bookish than него

note:
Не̏го and ве̏ћ are used only after a negation, in the sense «but rather».

Не̏го is also «than» in a comparison: ве̏ћӣ не̏го ја̑.

examples.en: Could I have a glass of white wine?
Bring a carafe of water to the table.

related.en: carafe, pitcher — several servings
glass of wine — a single serving in a glass

note: If you ask for бо̀ка̄л, a whole carafe is brought.

examples.en: I fell and I have a knee injury.

examples.sr: После тог догађаја остала је велика [тра̀ума].
examples.en: A great trauma remained after that event.

related.en: injury, damage — physical: a bruise, sprain, fracture
psychological trauma — shock, stress, an emotional mark

note: For a broken finger people say only по̏вреда, not тра̀ума.

examples.sr: [А̏ко] данас буде лепо време, идемо на Аду.
examples.en: If the weather is nice today, we'll go to Ada.

examples.sr: [Уколѝко̄] не платите рачун, услуга ће бити обустављена.
examples.en: If you do not pay the bill, the service will be suspended.

related.en: if — ordinary speech
in case, if — formal: instructions, contracts, notices

note: With a friend уколѝко̄ would sound like a letter from a bank.

examples.sr: Ишли смо право, [о̏нда̄] смо скренули лево.
examples.en: We went straight, then we turned left.

examples.sr: Најпре смо пили кафу, [по̀то̄м] смо шетали парком.
examples.en: First we had coffee, then we walked in the park.

related.en: then, so — colloquial
then, afterwards — more bookish: a story, a report

note: О̏нда̄ is also «then, in that case»: Ако хоћеш, онда иди.

examples.en: I love holidays because that is when I travel.
I love holidays because I get to rest.
I love holidays because of the gifts.

related.en: because — followed by a whole clause with a verb
because — shorter, also introduces a whole clause
because of — followed by a noun or pronoun in the genitive

note: Збо̏г takes only a noun: због кише. A whole clause is introduced by је̏р and за̀то̄ што̏.

examples.en: He speaks as if he were a Serb.
Do it the way I told you.

related.en: as if, as though — it seems so, but in fact it may be otherwise
as, such as — comparison, example

note: «Such as» is ка̏о што̏ су: воће као што су јагоде и брескве.

meanings: јутрос, вечерас, ноћас, синоћ, прексиноћ - when exactly

examples.en: I had coffee this morning.
We're going to the theater tonight.
I didn't sleep last night.
We watched a movie last night.
We were at a restaurant the night before last.

related.en: this morning
this evening, tonight
tonight or last night — depending on context
last night (evening or night)
the night before last (evening)

note: One word replaces a whole phrase: си̏но̄ћ instead of «yesterday evening».

examples.en: See you at six? - Works for me.
Talk tomorrow. - Deal.

examples.sr: Можеш ли да сачекаш пет минута? - [У ре̏ду].
examples.en: Can you wait five minutes? - All right.
So, Wednesday at eight? - It's settled!

examples.sr: То је добра идеја. - [Сла̏жем се], одлична је!
examples.en: That's a good idea. - I agree, it's great!
Will you come to lunch? - Of course!

examples.sr: Можеш ли ми позајмити књигу? - [Ка̏ко да не]!
examples.en: Can you lend me a book? - Sure thing!

related.en: works for me, sure — agreeing to a suggestion
okay, deal — confirming an arrangement
all right, fine — accepting a request or a situation
settled — a final arrangement
I agree — with someone's opinion
of course — without a shadow of doubt
sure thing, of course — willingly, with feeling

note: Ка̏ко да не said in an ironic tone can also mean «no way».

examples.en: We're preparing a celebration for Mom's birthday.

examples.sr: После победе у граду је почело велико [сла̑вље].
examples.en: After the victory, a big celebration began in the city.

examples.sr: Послао сам јој [че̏ститку] за Нову годину.
examples.en: I sent her a card for the New Year.

related.en: celebration, ceremony — a planned event
jubilation, festive merrymaking — joy, often spontaneous
greeting, greeting card — what is written or said on a holiday

note: To congratulate someone on a holiday is чести́тати.

meanings: платити with prefixes: доплатити, преплатити, потплатити, отплатити, уплатити

examples.sr: За пртљаг сам морала да [допла̀тим] двадесет евра.
examples.en: I had to pay twenty euros extra for my luggage.

examples.sr: Не желим да [препла̀тим] карту за концерт.
examples.en: I don't want to overpay for a concert ticket.
He tried to bribe the policeman.
We have been paying off the loan for seven years.
Today I paid the electricity bill.

related.en: to pay extra — pay the missing part or a fee for an additional service
to overpay — pay more than it is worth
to bribe — give a bribe (colloq.)
to pay off, repay — settle a debt in installments; also «to repay a kindness»
to pay in, make a payment — pay a bill, transfer money to an account

note: Отплатити and потпла́тити are easy to confuse: the first means to repay a debt, the second to give a bribe.

meanings: ћаскати, брбљати, ћућорити, беседити: ways of talking

examples.en: The neighbors were chatting in front of the building.
Stop babbling and listen!
The pupils are whispering at the back desk.
The professor gave a speech in front of a full hall.

related.en: to chat — lightly, in a friendly way, about nothing
to babble, prattle — a lot and out of place
to whisper to each other — under one's breath, e.g. in class
to hold forth, give a speech — solemn, bookish; jokingly of long stories

note: Бр̀бљати sounds reproachful, while ћа̏скати is warm and inoffensive.

meanings: кад, док or пре него што?

examples.en: When you arrive, let me know.
While everyone is talking, I'm making coffee.
Call me before you set off.

related.en: when — a moment or an event
while, as — two actions go on at the same time
before — an action that happens earlier than another

note: With a negation до̏к means «until»: чекај док не дођем - «wait until I come».

examples.en: I'm looking for a used phone up to a hundred euros.

examples.sr: Лекар је објаснио како делују [по̏лни] хормони.
examples.en: The doctor explained how sex hormones work.

related.en: used, second-hand — cars, equipment, clothes
sexual, of sex — related to sex (gender): полни хормони, полни органи

note: Not to be confused with пу̏н - «full».

examples.sr: У [недѐљу] идемо на ручак код баке.
examples.en: On Sunday we're going to Grandma's for lunch.
This week was hard for me.

related.en: Sunday — a day of the week: у недељу, недељом
week (seven days) — a period: ове седмице, пре две седмице

note: Нѐдеља means «Sunday». In speech it sometimes also means «week» (e.g. недељу дана), but for «week» сѐдмица is safer.

examples.en: He has ten years of experience in sales.
I like contemporary art.

related.en: experience — what has accumulated over the years: радно искуство
art — painting, music, theater

meanings: how to cook: кувати, пећи, динстати, пржити

examples.en: I'm boiling potatoes for the salad.
I'm baking fish in the oven.
I'm stewing vegetables in a little oil.
I'm frying fish in a pan.

related.en: to boil — in water: potatoes, pasta, soup, coffee
to bake, roast — in the oven: meat, vegetables, fish
to stew, braise — on low heat with some liquid: meat, vegetables
to fry — in oil: fish, eggs, potatoes

note: To say simply that you are cooking, use спре́мати: Шта̏ спре̑ма̄ш? - Спремам рибу («What are you making? - I'm making fish»).

examples.en: Which way is the main square?

examples.sr: Ово је једносмерна улица, само један [сме̑р].
examples.en: This is a one-way street, only one direction.

related.en: direction of travel (where to go or drive): у правцу центра
direction of traffic: једносмерна улица; also a track at school or university (a major)

examples.en: Look behind you, someone is following us.
I reversed the car into the parking spot.

related.en: back, backward — the direction behind, or a return: вратити се назад
reverse gear — of a car: укључити рикверц

note: A car moving backward is «у рикверц».

examples.en: Every morning I drive the kids to school.
This company imports fruit from Greece.

related.en: to drive away, take away — carry someone or something off
to bring in, import — into the country

examples.en: The mother is feeding the baby porridge.
I keep my documents in a drawer.

related.en: to feed, nourish — give food: children, pigeons
to keep, protect; look after — documents, children

examples.en: This is only a small part of the salary.
It is an honor to meet you.

related.en: part, share — a component of something: део града
honor; a treat — respect, esteem; a treat at the host's expense

note: Ча̑ст is «honor». Сва̏ка̄ ча̑ст! means «well done, bravo».

examples.en: After a long discussion we made a decision.

examples.sr: Полиција је ухапсила учеснике [о̏брачуна] међу бандама.
examples.en: The police arrested the participants of the gang showdown.

related.en: discussion, debate — in society, parliament, court: јавна расправа
settlement, calculation; showdown — counting up payments, or settling scores

note: Ра̑справа is a discussion, often a perfectly peaceful one. A violent settling of scores is о̏брачӯн.
